title: Consent-bounded Audit Gateway (CBD Audit Gateway) - PRD notes
content:
Purpose:
Provide a lightweight, consent-bounded audit gateway (CBD Gateway) for Private deployments that lets customers opt-in per-scope evidence capture while preserving the auditability required by our approval gates and attestation flows.

Notes / context (why this exists):
- Customers in regulated industries want narrow, explainable audit bundles tied to explicit consent or contractual scopes (e.g., SOC2, FINRA, health).
- Current private-deploy audit model (full event stream + long retention) is heavy on storage and creates privacy/scope friction for customers.
- We need a mechanism to produce minimal evidence capsules that satisfy approval decisions and post-incident forensics without exposing more telemetry than necessary.

High-level goals:
- Allow customers to define "consent scopes" (who/what/time) and map those scopes to audit capture policies.
- Produce compact, verifiable evidence capsules (signed, time-windowed) that can be consumed by approval gates, support, and customers.
- Support sampling and redaction heuristics so we capture signals for safety/regression while minimizing PII/excess telemetry.
- Integrate with existing approval flows so a failed approval or rollback can attach the minimal evidence needed for review.

Success metrics (initial):
- Evidence capsule size: median < 90KB for standard event windows
- Reduction in retained raw telemetry: 60% less compared to current default for customers that opt-in to consent-bounded mode
- Time-to-evidence: generation + signing < 4s at 95th percentile
- Adoption: 30% of new Private deployments choose consent-bounded mode in first 6 months (early adopters)

Scope (what this PRD covers):
- New gateway component (stateless edge service) deployed in Private (customer-managed) networks or in hybrid (control plane assisted) mode
- Consent token specification and API surfaces for customers to grant/revoke capture
- Sampling & redaction policy engine (config-driven)
- Evidence capsule format, signing, and upload/escrow API
- UX for operator and customer to review/consent captured artifacts

Out of scope (initial):
- Full SIEM integrations (we will add connectors after v1)
- Long-term archive & search UI (post-v1 work)

Architecture sketch (conceptual):
- Capture point: lightweight hooks in the control-plane agent and edge proxy that forward candidate audit events to the CBD Gateway
- CBD Gateway: evaluates event vs. consent token + sampling rules -> decides keep/redact/drop -> assembles evidence capsule
- Evidence Capsule Store: encrypted, signed capsules stored in customer-approved object store or escrowed to Redwood depending on config
- Approval gate integration: attach capsule id and signed proof to approval decisions for reviewers
- Customer consent manager: simple API + short-lived consent tokens (JWT-like) with scope claims

Component details / behaviors:
1) Consent tokens and semantics:
   - Tokens issued by customer or by control-plane on customer behalf (depends on private mode)
   - Claims: scope (resource ids, action types), time window, purpose (approval|forensic|sampling), owner id, retention hint
   - Revocation: short TTLs + revocation list support; gateway must stop capturing when token revoked
   - UX: customers can create one-off scopes (e.g., "can-capture-network-evidence-2025-09-01"), or templates for audits

2) Sampling & redaction policy engine:
   - Policy language: JSON DSL with matchers (resource, severity, user role), sample rate, redact rules (fields/keys), and fallback capture level
   - Default templates: "minimal forensic", "safety-sampling", "full-on-failure" (captures more if approval fails)
   - Live update: policies can be updated via API and pushed to gateways with eventual consistency

3) Evidence capsule format:
   - Flat JSON envelope with: capsule_id, time_window, scope_claims, event_digest_list (hashes), redacted_payloads (only allowed fields), provenance signature (sig of envelope)
   - For larger payloads, store blobs in encrypted object store and include references + integrity hashes in envelope
   - Signed with customer KMS or Redwood signing key depending on escrow setting

4) Approval gate integration:
   - Hook: when an approval decision is recorded, attach capsule_id(s) as supporting evidence
   - Auto-escalation: if approval fails, gateway may change sample rate to "full-on-failure" for next N minutes (configurable)

5) Privacy & retention:
   - Retention hints in token: gateway enforces minimum and maximum retention bounds declared in customer's config
   - Evidence capsules include a minimization audit: list of fields redacted and rationale (policy id)
   - Deletion flow: customer-initiated purge + verified deletion proof if stored on Redwood escrow (future)

Threat & risk model (high level):
- Risk: capsules expose sensitive info if policies misconfigured -> mitigate with conservative default redaction templates and warnings in UX
- Risk: revoked tokens still allow capture due to race -> gateway checks revocation list and applies TTL conservatively
- Risk: signing keys compromise -> support customer-managed KMS and rotate keys; short-term mitigation: capsule sigs include key metadata and rotation epoch

Operational requirements:
- Gateway must be deployable as a containerized service inside customer VPC, with optional host-network mode
- Minimal CPU/memory footprint; prefer streaming assembly of capsules to avoid large in-memory buffers
- Health endpoints + metrics: captures/sec, capsule-gen-latency, dropped-by-policy, revoked-token-attempts
- Debug mode for engineering: capture full trace locally with allowlist (never enabled by default in customer mode)

API surface (sketch):
- POST /consent-tokens -> returns token
- POST /capture-events -> event meta + token -> returns capsule_id or 202 if batched
- GET /capsule/{id} -> returns signed envelope (auth required)
- POST /policy -> update sampling/redaction templates (RBAC guarded)

Operator & customer UX:
- Customer console: create consent templates, view active tokens, inspect capsule metadata (hashes, size, policy used)
- Operator quickflow: when approving a change, UX surfaces "attached evidence capsule(s)" with redaction summary and link to download
- Audit log: immutable record (control-plane) linking approval decisions to capsule ids and token metadata

Rollout plan (phases):
- v0 (experiment): internal-only in staging; manual tokens; basic capsule format; short retention; no KMS
- v1 (private customers opt-in): deployable container, consent token API, sampling engine, capsule store support (S3-compatible), approval integration
- v1.1: KMS support for customer-managed keys, revocation list scaling, UI for templates
- v2: SIEM connectors, search index, evidence escrow SLA

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should tokens be single-use for highest-sensitivity scopes? Pros/cons on UX
- Where to store revocation list for low-latency checks in entirely air-gapped customers? (local cache + periodic sync?)
- Acceptance criteria for "minimal forensic" template (we need concrete field lists from legal/compliance)
- Retention SLA options: what granularity to expose in UI (days/weeks/months)
- Logging: do we surface policy-match reasons in capsule or keep them internal? (privacy vs explainability tradeoff)

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Product: draft full policy DSL spec (Rahul) - due 2025-09-12
- Eng - serving-runtime: prototype gateway dispatcher hooking into control-plane agent (Samir) - spike by 2025-09-05
- Security & Legal: provide initial minimal forensic field list and compliance checklist (Eleanor) - by 2025-09-19
- UX: wireframes for consent token flow and attach evidence view (Marina + Jordan) - first pass 2025-09-10

Appendix / quick examples:
- Example token claim: {\"scope\": [\"vpc:net-abc\"], \"purpose\": \"approval\", \"from\": \"2025-09-01T00:00:00Z\", \"to\": \"2025-09-01T04:00:00Z\", \"retention_days\": 30}
- Example minimal capsule envelope (summary): {\"capsule_id\": \"cap_123\", \"time_window\": \"2025-09-01T00:00:00Z/2025-09-01T00:05:00Z\", \"policy_id\": \"min_forensic_v0\", \"event_hashes\": [\"h1\", \"h2\"], \"redaction_summary\": [\"removed: src_ip\"], \"signature\": \"sig_v1\"}

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight and focused on the capture+consent primitives; tie back to existing approval-gate PRDs. We should not duplicate the attestation signing work but reuse key formats where possible.

References: see linked artifacts for initial tickets and a working Confluence page.
